parsed.main_gap: Lemma 4 falsely infers that the whole graph is acyclic from |E|<|V|; a cycle may coexist with isolated vertices. The argument is repaired by choosing any component with fewer edges than vertices.

errors.description: The graph-theoretic inference is false: one cyclic component and isolated vertices can have fewer total edges than vertices. However, averaging over components guarantees some connected component T has |E_T|<|V_T|, hence is a tree; using that T instead of the component containing n completes the argument.
errors.quote: Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible.

parsed.notes: The stated answer, picking-game reduction, geometric lower-bound framework, and subset-sum/cross-pairing upper bound are otherwise rigorous. The sole serious flaw is local and straightforwardly repairable.
